title: Dedicated SKU Value Map for CISO & Finance — SLAs, Isolation, Throughput
body:
Purpose
This is a concise messaging and negotiation playbook tailored to two procurement personas — CISO/security decision makers and finance/FP&A buyers — focused on Redwood’s Dedicated capacity SKU (reserved GPU pools). Goal: give field reps and AEs short, procurement-ready language, risk framing, and checklist items that map to legal/finance asks.

High-level positioning summary (one-liners)
- For CISOs: 'Dedicated pools with client-controlled boundaries, auditable key management, and deterministic failure modes — designed for compliance and forensics without sacrificing latency SLAs.'
- For Finance: 'Predictable per-month committed capacity with usage smoothing, transparent unit economics, and fallback policies to avoid surprise overages.'

Key value themes to lead with (persona-specific)
1) CISO / Security Lead
- Isolation guarantees: single-tenant GPU pools + network segmentation. Say: "logical and physical isolation options; VPC peering or on-prem appliance available."
- Auditability & keys: KMS/HSM integration, audit logs surfaced in Console + long-retention export.
- Data residency & controls: region pinning and optional on-prem package for regulated workloads.
- Deterministic incident behavior: clear failover playbooks and sandboxed cold-starts to reduce blast radius.
- Ask we solve: provide a contractable control surface (controls + evidence) so InfoSec can sign off without building a custom stack.

2) Finance / Procurement Lead
- Predictable spend: committed monthly/annual reserved SKU priced to smooth token-unit costs vs bursty usage.
- Unit economics transparency: sample cost per 1M tokens at common batch sizes + guidance on quantization/batching tradeoffs.
- Negotiation levers: Minimum term, burst buffer quantity, overage rates, and true-up cadence. Present options (A/B) for elasticity vs price.
- Ask we solve: reduce forecast variance and provide clear fallbacks instead of open cloud runaway spend.

Top-level objections and short rebuttals
- "We can self-host cheaper." -> "Self-hosting shifts ops, reliability and amortized engineering costs onto your team; Dedicated SKU gives SLA-backed uptime and predictable throughput with OPEX-friendly monthly pricing plus operational SLAs you can contract against."
- "How do we know isolation is real?" -> "We provide network diagrams, deployment templates, and an independent attestation checklist. For the highest assurance customers we can propose an on-site proof-of-concept and generate a security review pack (KMS config, audit exports, host allocation logs)."
- "What if we spike beyond committed capacity?" -> "Agreement includes configured burst capacity and controlled fallback rules; we’ll route to compatible, lower-cost pools or throttle gracefully per contractual thresholds to avoid degraded availability or surprise charges."

Procurement-ready checklist (what to include in SOW / contract asks)
- SLA specifics: availability % by region, p99/p95 latency targets, measured token throughput targets. Define measurement method and reporting cadence.
- Isolation & tenancy clause: physical/tenant isolation description and definitions of "dedicated" vs "shared" in contract language.
- Data treatment: encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest, KMS key ownership options (customer-managed key).
- Incident response: RTO/RPO expectations, notification timelines, post-incident report deliverables.
- Capacity management: committed capacity units, burst allowances, scaling windows, overage billing rates and true-up process.
- Audit & compliance deliverables: monthly audit logs export, SOC/ISO artifacts (if available), penetration test summaries or third-party attestations.
- Termination & data exit: data egress process, retention / deletion timeline, and assistance for model artifacts export.

Playbook snippets for Sales/AE (talk tracks)
- Intro call (CISO): "We designed Dedicated to be an isolatable runtime you can validate via our security pack. If you prioritize deterministic SLA-backed inference and want to avoid building an internal stack, we handle the runtime and operational risk. What are your compliance gates?"
- Intro call (Finance): "Companies move to Dedicated when forecasting and unit-cost predictability matter. We’ll model your steady-state committed spend and show a plan for smoothing peaks via burst allowances. How do you currently forecast inference spend?"
- Negotiation framing: present a 'Safe Starter' term: 12-month commitment with a modest burst pool and 30-day true-up; include an option to convert to enterprise annual coverage with volume discounts.

Competitive callouts (how to differentiate succinctly)
- Against large cloud-hosted model APIs: emphasize tenancy semantics and SLA granularity. Many public APIs lack contractual throughput guarantees or per-tenant isolation commitments.
- Against self-hosted inference vendors: emphasize the operational SLAs, ongoing runtime optimizations (continuous kernel tuning, batching/kv caching improvements), and a productized rollouts/observability experience; we shoulder runtime upgrades and scaling risk.
- Against boutique inference infra providers: call out Redwood’s breadth — hosted + dedicated + private parity — and the product-level controls for rollouts and cost tooling.

Examples & numbers (to include in sales materials) — fill with customer-specific inputs in playbook runbooks
- Example A (mid-market SaaS): 20M tokens/day steady; 40M bursts twice weekly. Suggested commitment: 4x GPU pool reserved with 25% burst buffer. Estimated blended per-token unit cost: $X (include model + infra + ops).
- Example B (enterprise regulated): Contract: 12-month reserved capacity, HSM-backed keys, SOC artifact delivery, monthly throughput reports with 99.9% availability SLA.

Open items & asks to product/legal before next field roll-out
- Define precise SLA measurement window and tooling (what Console metrics will be contractually authoritative).
- Create a security evidence packet template (exportable) for in-person audits / procurement docs.
- Standardize contract language for "burst buffer" and overage math so AEs can push a single sentence into SOW.
- Price table: build a slide with 3 sample commitment tiers and modeled per-token costs across different batch sizes.

Quick reference snippets for proposal docs (copy/paste)
- "Redwood Dedicated provides a contract-backed, single-tenant inference pool with configurable burst capacity and audit-grade logs. Customer-managed keys and region pinning supported. SLA: 99.9% availability and p95 latency ≤ 150ms for configured model families."
- "Overage handling: traffic beyond committed units will first use the configured burst buffer; sustained excess triggers a true-up at the agreed overage rate defined in Section 3.2 of the SOW."

Notes to field / conversation starters for legal
- We should offer a standard 12-month and 36-month SOW template. Longer commitments get steeper volume discounts and an SLA escalation path.
- Add a standard security appendix that enumerates artifacts we can or cannot provide (e.g., we can provide SOC reports, but not raw host logs without a subpoena).

Appendix: sample questions we expect from procurement
- "What exactly constitutes a breach of SLA?" -> Provide measurement windows, partial credit calculations, and remediation credits.
- "Can we run a PoC in our VPC?" -> Yes, limited PoC terms available; define duration and capacity.
- "How do keys get rotated?" -> Customer-managed keys supported; document rotation cadence and support handoffs.

Quick next steps
- Finalize security evidence packet and get sign-off from security by 2025-08-09.
- Product to confirm the SLA measurement metric and Console authoritative API by 2025-08-05.
- Create draft SOW language for burst buffer and overage math and circulate to Legal by 2025-08-07.

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Keep examples numeric but high-level; ops will fill real numbers per customer.
- Need one-slide SKU mapping (term / burst / per-token model) for AE enablement.

References and links
- Internal: GTM-2339 (bundle for dedicated pricing), security pack draft (Confluence: DED-SKU-SEC-PACK), existing Dedicated SOW template in Legal drive.
- External comps: internal brief on cloud-hosted vendors vs self-hosted economics (link in Slack thread above).

End.
